target_definition.metric: United States monthly core CPI change

graph_diagnosis.summary: Energy costs, shelter inflation, broader disinflation, and services-price pressure form a reusable core-inflation framework.
weaknesses: Energy is excluded directly from core CPI and operates indirectly.
Annual-rate evidence is an imperfect proxy for the monthly calculation.

search_factors.why_search: Energy costs can affect transport and production expenses that feed into core goods and services.
Shelter is a large core-CPI component and its pace materially affects core inflation.
Aggregate disinflation links component price changes to the core CPI trend.
Persistent services price pressure can offset easing in shelter and energy-related costs.
Headline inflation can signal countervailing food, energy, and goods price movements.

checkpoints.mechanism: Lower energy costs can reduce transportation and production expenses.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Track retail fuel prices and business-cost pass-through.

checkpoints.mechanism: Moderating shelter-price growth reduces pressure in a large core component.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Check monthly shelter inflation and rental measures.

checkpoints.mechanism: Lower cost pressures and shelter moderation combine into broader disinflation.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Reconcile component changes with core CPI.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Component easing fails to affect core services.

checkpoints.mechanism: Persistent services inflation can resist broader disinflation.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Track services PPI and core-services CPI.

checkpoints.mechanism: Headline price increases can coexist with easing in core components.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Compare food and energy effects with core components.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Headline and core move together due to services.

checkpoints.mechanism: Shelter and other core-component changes aggregate into monthly core CPI.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Use the published core CPI level to calculate the monthly percentage change.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Component narrative does not reconcile to the published index.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Lower cost pressure can contribute indirectly to softer core-component inflation.
applicability_conditions: Business cost reductions pass through to core goods and services.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Shelter moderation reduces a major source of core-inflation pressure.
applicability_conditions: Shelter has material weight in the monthly index.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Persistent services inflation offsets shelter moderation.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminating_evidence: Compare core-services components with shelter and goods inflation.

forecast_audit_questions: Is shelter inflation continuing to moderate?
Are energy-cost changes passing through to core components?
Does services inflation offset easing elsewhere?
Do component changes reconcile to the published monthly core CPI level?
